context.title: A cited answer isn't the same as a checked answer
context.body: Vera answers clinical questions with citations from millions of papers and guidelines, and grades the evidence. But a clinician on a ward has seconds to decide whether to trust a line. Citations sit at the level of the answer, not the claim, so checking means opening a source and hunting for the passage. Local protocols can differ from national guidance, and some users say they can't open a reference at the exact page.
assumptions: I haven't used Vera. My view comes from a detailed 2026 review, Google Play reviews and the job post, so the product may already do some of this.
Clinical content is illustrative, based on ATS/IDSA 2019 and NICE NG138 outpatient pneumonia guidance; 'St Luke's antimicrobial guide' is fictional. Not medical advice.
Vera's own visuals weren't available to inspect; this uses a calm clinical style (white, deep navy, teal). No Vera logo.
Per-claim matching assumes Vera can align answer sentences to source passages, which its retrieval likely supports.

goals.title: Check any line in one tap
goals.body: Each claim shows whether its source supports it, and the exact passage.

goals.title: Show where certainty differs
goals.body: Evidence grade per claim, not one grade for the whole answer.

goals.title: Respect local protocols
goals.body: Flag where the hospital's guide differs, and open it at the page.

jtbd: When I look something up between patients, I want to check the line I'm about to act on in seconds, so I can trust the answer without reading the whole paper.

evidence.finding: A 2026 review notes 'a citation does not prove that the source supports the claim', and that evidence grading 'may differ between statements in one answer'.
The same review says country-aware answers 'need checking against national and local guidance'. Vera Spaces combine internal protocols with external guidance.
A Google Play reviewer (Aug 2026) says local sources lack a file reader 'to view the exact page of the reference'. Vera has 4.8 stars from about 11K reviews and 100K+ downloads.

source.label: Google Play: Vera Health, AI for Clinicians

evidence.finding: Every screen should help a clinician 'understand what they're looking at, find what they need, and know what to do next'.

approaches: Inline citations with an evidence grade
Show the exact passage in a sheet
Open sources at the right page

ranges.title: Sources at the end
ranges.summary: Answer text, then a list of sources.
cons: No link from a line to its source.

ranges.title: Inline citations
ranges.summary: A citation number and evidence grade on each sentence.
pros: Shows where each line came from.
cons: No sign the source really supports it.

ranges.title: Claim Check
ranges.summary: Each claim is labelled Supported or Partly supported, with its evidence grade; tap to see the exact passage highlighted; local protocol differences are flagged with a link to the page.
pros: Checking takes one tap, not a search.
cons: More UI on a small screen.

decision.title: Claim Check: every line, one tap from its proof
decision.body: Range 3. Answers split into claims, each with a support label and evidence grade. Tapping a claim opens a sheet with the exact passage highlighted and, when support is partial, why. When the user's hospital protocol differs, Vera says so and opens the guide at the page.
reasons: Clinicians act on single lines, so trust has to work at that level.
Being open about partial support builds more trust than hiding it.
Local protocols are what many clinicians actually have to follow.
decision.tradeoff: Matching a claim to a passage can be wrong. I'd show the passage itself, never just a score, so the clinician can judge.

depth.body: Built as a working iPhone screen. A question about outpatient pneumonia gets three claims, each marked Supported or Partly supported with its evidence grade. Tapping the duration claim opens a sheet with the guideline passage highlighted and a note on why it's only partly supported. A hospital protocol that uses a different dose is flagged with a link to its page. The sheet slides up, and motion turns off for people who reduce it.

validation.method: I'd watch five clinicians use Vera between patients and time how long they take to check a line, then test Claim Check against today's answers.
hypotheses: Clinicians open sources more often, and faster.
Fewer answers are flagged as wrong or misleading.
Trust ratings rise for answers with partial support shown.

metrics.name: Time to verify
metrics.definition: Seconds from answer to viewing the supporting passage.

metrics.name: Source opens per answer
metrics.definition: How often clinicians open a cited passage.

metrics.name: Flag rate
metrics.definition: Claims flagged by users per 1,000 answers.
